claims.publisher: Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost (NÚKIB), Sbírka zákonů ČR
claims.quote: Zákaznická data a specifické provozní údaje jsou zpracovávány na území České republiky.
claims.quote_english: Customer data and specific operational data are processed on the territory of the Czech Republic (Annex 4, requirement 1.2, critical security level).
claims.title: Vyhláška č. 505/2025 Sb., o některých požadavcích pro zápis do katalogu cloud computingu, příloha č. 4

indicators.research_note: Binding rules set jurisdiction only for the highest-risk tier. Under Act 365/2000 § 6m(2), public administration cloud workloads at the highest ('kritická') security level may be hosted only by the state-designated state cloud provider. NÚKIB Decree 505/2025 (in force since 1.1.2026, replacing Decree 316/2021) Annex 4 requires processing in the Czech Republic at the critical level, with narrow justified exceptions. Lower levels require only a provider seat or representative in the EU (§ 3), and EU/EFTA storage is a declared option there, not a mandate. No statute requiring national or EU jurisdiction for government data in general was found. Cybersecurity Act 264/2025 was searched and has no data-location clause. Hence partial.

review.reason: Both quotes appear verbatim. § 6m(2) of Act 365/2000 reserves highest-level cloud to the state provider, and Annex 4 row 1.2 of Decree 505/2025 requires critical-level data to be processed in the Czech Republic, but only for the top tier and not for government data in general, which fits partial.

indicators.research_note: § 4 of Act 412/2005 sets out four classification levels in statute: Přísně tajné, Tajné, Důvěrné and Vyhrazené. Unclassified public-administration systems also get statutory security levels (nízká, střední, vysoká, kritická) for cloud use under Act 365/2000 and Act 264/2025, with NÚKIB implementing decrees.

review.reason: § 4 of Act 412/2005 appears verbatim and sets out four statutory classification levels (Přísně tajné, Tajné, Důvěrné, Vyhrazené).

claims.quote: Poskytovatelem cloud computingu poskytujícím orgánu veřejné správy cloud computing zařazený do nejvyšší bezpečnostní úrovně může být pouze poskytovatel státního cloud computingu.
claims.quote_english: Only the state cloud computing provider may provide a public administration body with cloud computing classified at the highest security level.
claims.title: Zákon č. 365/2000 Sb., o informačních systémech veřejné správy, § 6m odst. 2

indicators.research_note: Czechia has a binding, in-force cloud qualification scheme: the cloud computing catalogue (katalog cloud computingu) with four security levels under Act 365/2000 and NÚKIB Decree 505/2025. It is not a SecNumCloud-type certification. For commercial providers, even at the critical level (Annex 4, row 2.2), it requires only disclosure of obligations under non-EU law, not immunity from them. The sovereignty safeguard is structural instead: the highest level is reserved by statute for the state-established state cloud provider (§ 6m(2)), and critical-level processing must take place in the Czech Republic. I rated this partial because an in-force scheme addresses the risk without an immunity criterion. A stricter reading could score it 'no', but no source states outright that no immunity certification exists. Web search budget ran out; I did not find a NÚKIB statement on EUCS or on immunity.

review.reason: The row 2.2 quote is on the page, but it requires only disclosure of obligations under non-EU law, not immunity from them, and § 6m(2) is not a certification, so no cited source shows that an immunity-requiring certification exists at all, whether adopted or required; since a 'no' is not permitted without a source saying so, this goes to unknown.

claims.quote: Správa byla ze strany Digitální a informační agentury zapsána na Seznam kvalifikovaných poskytovatelů služeb vytvářejících důvěru a poskytovaných kvalifikovaných služeb vytvářejících důvěru a od 1. ledna 2024 může poskytovat služby vytvářející důvěru.

claims.title: Úvodní strana – Správa státních služeb vytvářejících důvěru

indicators.research_note: The Czech Trusted List (https://tsl.gov.cz/publ/TSL_CZ.xtsl) is operated by the Digitální a informační agentura. Among its qualified TSPs are the state body 'Správa státních služeb vytvářejících důvěru' (trade name Národní certifikační autorita, NCA), 'Správa základních registrů' and the state enterprise Česká pošta, s.p. (PostSignum). Private qualified TSPs are also listed: I.CA, eIdentity, Software602, SEFIRA, TECHNISERV IT, Komerční banka and Seyfor. The XML trusted list is not quoted because its tag structure breaks up the text. The government's own qualified trust service is operated by a state organisation set up by statute.

review.reason: § 14(1) and (4) of Act 297/2016 appear verbatim: they establish the Správa as a state contributory organisation (founded by the Agentura) that provides trust services for the Czech Republic, and sssvd.gov.cz confirms it has been on the qualified list since 1 Jan 2024.

indicators.research_note: The national eID hub (Národní bod / NIA, Identita občana) is a public administration information system. § 20(2) of Act 250/2017 names the Agentura (the state Digitální a informační agentura, DIA) as its administrator. The state-issued means are the chip ID card, NIA ID and Mobilní klíč eGovernmentu. Bank iDs issued by private parties plug into the state hub as additional qualified means. The eIDAS notified-schemes list was not fetched, because the EC page renders with JavaScript.

review.reason: All three quotes are on their pages. § 20(1) makes the National Point a public administration system, § 20(2) names the state Agentura as its administrator, and identitaobcana.cz describes NIA ID as provided by the state.

indicators.research_note: SPCSS is a state enterprise (s. p.) of the Ministry of Finance. It runs two government data centres: DC Vápenka in Prague and the new DC Zeleneč, both Tier III. The live site spcss.cz blocks automated requests with HTTP 403, so the claim cites a Wayback Machine snapshot of the official homepage from 14 May 2026. The state enterprise NAKIT (Ministry of Interior) also runs government infrastructure, but nakit.cz blocked access.

review.reason: The archived official SPCSS (state enterprise, s. p.) homepage contains the quote verbatim and names two operating data centres, DC Vápenka (Tier III, Prague) and DC Zeleneč.

claims.title: Zákon č. 365/2000 Sb., o informačních systémech veřejné správy, § 6i odst. 1 písm. a)

indicators.research_note: The eGovernment Cloud rests on Act 365/2000, Head VI. Its state part (Státní část eGovernment cloudu) is run by SPCSS, which the Government designated as state cloud provider on 20 Dec 2023. SPCSS describes itself as the provider of this service to state administration, and § 6m(2) makes it the only lawful host for critical-level workloads. DIA's Informační systém cloud computingu (ISCC, the catalogue system, not a hosting platform) went live on 1 July 2026. No usage statistics on workloads were retrieved, so the 'serving government workloads' element rests on the operator's own description.

review.reason: The DIA archive says verbatim that the Government designated SPCSS as state cloud provider on 20 Dec 2023, the SPCSS homepage describes it in the present tense as the provider of the State part of the eGovernment cloud to the state administration, and § 6i(1)(a) is verbatim; this supports an operating platform, though workload use rests on the operator's own statement.
